name: Allocate capital and set program mandates and deployment guidance
summary: Total Fund Management decides how much capital each of about 20 active investment programs should target, at what pace it should deploy and with what risk, regional and sector characteristics, and the Chief Investment Officer approves each program's written mandate. In the annual round after the Strategic Portfolio is approved, and in quarterly updates as markets and pipelines change, staff compile each program's deployment and pipeline, compare the sum with the total fund targets and liquidity budget, ask departments for updated requests and draft allocations. Department heads in Private Equity, Real Assets, Credit, Active Equities and Capital Markets review and contest their numbers, a TFM managing director negotiates, and the CIO approves the mandates and guidance. Elapsed time goes mostly to waiting for department inputs and negotiation rounds, and stale program data is the main error source.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national pension fund investment manager whose Total Fund Management department allocates capital to active programs run by five investment departments and completes the exposures with a balancing portfolio.
baseline.notes: The Active Portfolio Management group had about 12 people in this model; the round is one of several activities of the group.

trigger: A new Strategic Portfolio is approved (annual round) or quarter-end performance and pipeline data arrive (quarterly update).
end_state: Approved program mandates and deployment guidance are issued to departments, loaded into the data and risk platforms, and the balancing team and Risk are briefed.

volume.seasonality: The annual round in March to April carries most of the work; quarterly updates follow quarter-end performance reporting. Occasional extra rounds when a large deal or market move forces a reallocation.

evidence.note: Annual guidance to the investment groups (F2021); quarterly refresh and extra rounds are the process map's assumption.

steps.name: Open the allocation round
steps.description: The Active Portfolio Management director confirms whether this round is the annual mandate refresh after the Strategic Portfolio is approved or a quarterly guidance update after quarter-end performance, sets the timetable and tells departments what will be asked of them.

evidence.note: Departments receive annual guidance; TFM refreshes it as markets and pipelines change. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Compile program deployment and pipeline data
steps.description: A senior associate pulls each program's net assets, returns, deployment against its range, unfunded commitments and pipeline from the performance report, the data platform and the deal pipeline system into the allocation workbook.

error.defect_description: A program's unfunded commitments or pipeline are taken from a stale extract.

evidence.note: Guidance covers targeted size and short-term deployment targets for each program. Effort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check program figures against Finance data
steps.description: The senior associate compares program totals with the performance and accounting figures, investigates differences in program mapping or timing and fixes the workbook or logs the break with Finance.

error.defect_description: A mapping difference is accepted without explanation.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common reconciliation of planning data with reported results.

steps.name: Analyse total fund fit
steps.description: A principal aggregates the programs' expected exposures over one and five years, compares them with the Strategic Portfolio and current-year targets by factor, region and asset class, and checks the liquidity budget for private deployments.

error.defect_description: A program's factor mapping is out of date, distorting the gap analysis.

evidence.note: Allocations must collectively deliver the desired factor, regional and sector exposures and preserve total portfolio liquidity, which must cover investment funding needs. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Ask departments for updated pipelines and requests
steps.description: The senior associate sends each department's business management team the gap analysis extract and a template for updated pipelines, capacity and any requested change to program size or range.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Consolidate department requests
steps.description: As the five departments reply, the senior associate chases late ones, puts requests on a common basis and lists where the requested capital exceeds what the total fund can absorb.

error.defect_description: A request is recorded on a gross rather than net basis.

evidence.note: Signals take account of departments' business and investment plans. Response time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Draft proposed allocations and deployment guidance
steps.description: The principal sets for each program a target size, deployment range, intended risk and characteristics by region, sector and investment type, and expected return spread, trading off department requests against total fund gaps and liquidity.

error.defect_description: A deployment range is inconsistent with the program's target size path.

evidence.note: The business plan sets Target Portfolio allocation bands; Investment Department signals specify intended risk and characteristics, contributions to exposures, five-year target size, short-term deployment targets, expected returns and return spreads. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Revise allocations after negotiation
steps.description: When the negotiation leaves several departments unresolved, the principal revises the disputed program sizes and ranges, rechecks the total fund fit and liquidity budget, and recirculates the revised proposal to department heads.

error.defect_description: A revised range breaks the liquidity budget agreed earlier.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; a second round changes only the disputed programs.

steps.name: Director reviews the proposal
steps.description: The Active Portfolio Management director reviews the proposed allocations for consistency with the Strategic Portfolio and fairness across departments and sends the principal back to rework any that will not hold up.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Private Equity head reviews proposed allocation
steps.description: The global head of Private Equity reviews the proposed target sizes, deployment ranges and characteristics for the department's fund, secondary, co-investment and direct private equity programs, compares them with the department's pipeline and business plan, and replies with acceptance or objections and supporting deal evidence.

evidence.note: Departments receive guidance on target size and deployment and are accountable for proposing or resizing strategies within ISRC approvals. Times are the author's estimates; reviews run in parallel.

steps.name: Real Assets head reviews proposed allocation
steps.description: The global head of Real Assets reviews the proposed target sizes, deployment ranges and characteristics for the department's real estate, infrastructure and sustainable energy programs, compares them with the department's pipeline and business plan, and replies with acceptance or objections and supporting deal evidence.

evidence.note: Departments receive guidance on target size and deployment and are accountable for proposing or resizing strategies within ISRC approvals. Times are the author's estimates; reviews run in parallel.

steps.name: Credit Investments head reviews proposed allocation
steps.description: The global head of Credit Investments reviews the proposed target sizes, deployment ranges and characteristics for the department's private and public credit programs, compares them with the department's pipeline and business plan, and replies with acceptance or objections and supporting deal evidence.

evidence.note: Departments receive guidance on target size and deployment and are accountable for proposing or resizing strategies within ISRC approvals. Times are the author's estimates; reviews run in parallel.

steps.name: Active Equities head reviews proposed allocation
steps.description: The global head of Active Equities reviews the proposed target sizes, deployment ranges and characteristics for the department's fundamental, relationship and thematic equity programs, compares them with the department's pipeline and business plan, and replies with acceptance or objections and supporting deal evidence.

evidence.note: Departments receive guidance on target size and deployment and are accountable for proposing or resizing strategies within ISRC approvals. Times are the author's estimates; reviews run in parallel.

steps.name: Capital Markets and Factor Investing head reviews proposed allocation
steps.description: The global head of Capital Markets and Factor Investing reviews the proposed target sizes, deployment ranges and characteristics for the department's external manager, macro and systematic programs, compares them with the department's pipeline and business plan, and replies with acceptance or objections and supporting deal evidence.

evidence.note: Departments receive guidance on target size and deployment and are accountable for proposing or resizing strategies within ISRC approvals. Times are the author's estimates; reviews run in parallel.

steps.name: Negotiate disputed allocations
steps.description: A TFM managing director meets the department heads who objected, weighs their deal evidence against total fund needs and agrees revised numbers, or sends the proposal back for a further round when several departments disagree.

evidence.note: Department heads negotiate allocations, so the work needs several rounds (process map); competition for capital. Share and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Draft program mandates and guidance letters
steps.description: A senior associate updates each affected program's written mandate (scope of investments, comparative advantage, strategies, measures of success) and writes the department guidance letters with the agreed sizes, ranges and deployment targets.

error.defect_description: A letter repeats last round's range for one program.

evidence.note: Written mandates specify scope, comparative advantages, strategies and measures of success. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Managing director reviews the mandate package
steps.description: The TFM managing director checks the mandate changes and letters against what was agreed in the negotiations and clears the package for the CIO.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: CIO approves mandates and guidance
steps.description: The Chief Investment Officer reviews the package, usually at a Portfolio Strategy Committee meeting, resolves any escalated disagreement and approves the written mandates and the guidance.

control.basis: Total portfolio framework: every investment program needs a written mandate approved by the CIO

evidence.note: Written mandates approved by the CIO (F2021); the CIO chairs the PSC (F2022). Wait and rework share are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Issue mandates and guidance to departments
steps.description: The director sends each department head its approved mandates and guidance letter, walks business management teams through the changes and files the signed documents.

evidence.note: Each department receives clear annual guidance. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Update program targets in systems
steps.description: The senior associate loads the new program targets and ranges into the data platform and risk platform used for balancing, PEC fit checks and monitoring, and a colleague checks the loaded values.

error.defect_description: A range is keyed against the wrong program code.

control.basis: Four-eyes check of target and reference data changes

evidence.note: Author's estimate of how approved targets reach daily systems.

steps.name: Brief balancing and Risk on target changes
steps.description: A principal tells the balancing team which completion exposures will change as programs grow or shrink and gives Risk the new program ranges for its monitoring, then closes the round.

evidence.note: Balancing programs are traded so that, with the active portfolio, the fund keeps its targeted risk and factor exposures. Times are the author's estimates.

exceptions.name: Second negotiation round
exceptions.description: Several departments reject their allocations, so the principal redrafts and departments review again before the CIO sees the package.

exceptions.name: Director sends proposal back
exceptions.description: The director finds an allocation that is inconsistent with the Strategic Portfolio or unfair across departments and asks for rework before departments see it.

exceptions.name: Out-of-cycle reallocation for a large transaction
exceptions.description: A department needs room for a large deal before the next round; a smaller version of the round runs for the affected programs, with the CIO approving the change.

exceptions.name: CIO changes the package
exceptions.description: The CIO resolves an escalation differently from the proposal and the mandate documents are redrafted.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from opening the round to issuing mandates
benchmarks.population: Program allocation rounds at a large Canadian pension investment manager

evidence.note: Author's estimate: a round must finish well inside the quarter it guides, with two to three weeks for department inputs, one or two negotiation rounds and a committee date.
Active programs about 65% of gross assets; balancing programs complete the exposures.

pain_points.description: Department heads contest allocations with competing ambitions, so rounds repeat and the CIO arbitrates escalations.

evidence.note: Departments propose and resize strategies; competition for capital.

pain_points.description: Pipeline and unfunded commitment data come from several systems and departments, so figures are stale or on different bases.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common data issues in allocation planning.

pain_points.description: Waiting for department replies and the committee date takes most of the elapsed time.

evidence.note: Author's reading of the step chain.

sources.title: The model fund F2022 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2022)
sources.supports: Strategic Portfolios: six asset classes and three regions, indicative allocations five years out (base plan public equity 23%, private equity 23%, public fixed income 32%, credit 17%, real assets 31%, cash and absolute return -27%); strategic mix of factor exposures and leverage reviewed at least triennially; CIO accountable for designing Strategic Portfolios and recommending market risk and leverage targets; ISRC with Portfolio Execution, Portfolio Strategy, Investment Risk and Operational and Legal Risk committees; Business Plan includes the Strategic Portfolios; leverage defined (term debt, commercial paper, secured borrowing, synthetic financing); recourse leverage C$122 billion in F2022, 18% to 25% of net assets over five years; Board limit of 45% of net assets from April 1, 2022, reviewed yearly with risk appetite; 10-day liquidity coverage ratio 2.9x against 1.0x; leverage-related expenses C$295 million. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: The model fund F2021 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2021)
sources.supports: TFM responsibilities (Strategic Exposures, current-year target exposures and range expectations, alignment of departments); Active Portfolio Management gives annual factor, geographic and sector guidance to 20 investment programs; Portfolio Design sets targeted allocation to programs within risk appetite and liquidity constraints; TFM's annual portfolio design process with departments and Risk over one- and five-year periods narrows each program to a preferred five-year deployment range; Balancing and Collateral group delivers required financial leverage; FCT executes financing and the term debt programme; External Portfolio Management has more than 60 managers and negotiates fees for alignment. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: The model fund 2020 Annual Report
sources.supports: Board governance of investment strategy: Risk Policy and risk appetite approved annually, Reference Portfolios, Business Plan with confirmation or adjustment of the Strategic Portfolios and Target Portfolios' allocation bands, Investment Statements; Board approves external manager appointments as required by the Act, delegating to the CEO those below a defined size; five key return-risk factors used in portfolio construction. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: Statement of Investment Objectives, Policies, Return Expectations and Risk Management for the Investment Portfolios of the Base plan and the Additional plan (version effective April 2, 2025)
sources.supports: Strategic Portfolios at Reference Portfolio risk (s. 5.3), reviewed at least triennially (s. 5.4), target allocations reviewed annually; Board approves market risk, liquidity and leverage limits annually (ss. 9.2, 9.5); leverage limits are a maximum relative to net assets; liquidity practices cover debt service, margin and transactions (s. 9.6); debt may be issued through a dedicated subsidiary with a guarantee (s. 8); transactions and external manager engagements above Board-set limits need ISC approval (s. 9.9). Later than the reference period; used for practice. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: From Vision to Execution: How investors are operationalizing the total portfolio approach
sources.publisher: Thinking Ahead Institute, WTW and CAIA Association
sources.supports: Total portfolio approach practice: at the model fund a central investment committee coordinates capital allocation across asset classes and a central portfolio construction group brings exposures together; competition for capital based on marginal contribution to the total portfolio; reference portfolios as the board's risk anchor. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

assumptions: The five department head reviews run in parallel; they are listed in sequence with near-zero waits after the first and marked concurrent.
Department business management teams' time on submissions is not counted; it shows as the wait at s06.
The process map lists no Risk role; Risk's view enters through the Strategic Portfolio and the monitoring briefing at s20.
Trigger shares assume one annual round triggered by the Strategic Portfolio and three quarterly updates triggered by performance reporting.
The CIO's approval is assumed to happen at a Portfolio Strategy Committee meeting; the organisation does not publish this cadence.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file.
